barriers.description: Clinicians' limited availability and short meeting times prevented full participation in design sessions.
barriers.justification: This constrained facilitation of user involvement and coordination of the multidisciplinary team, limiting designers' ability to manage user understanding and integrate feedback across iterations.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Challenges included time constraints as meetings were scheduled for only 1 hour and not all clinicians could fully participate in all design sessions.

barriers.description: Not all user groups were directly involved in the design process, creating gaps in representation.
barriers.justification: Incomplete user representation hindered designers' ability to fully understand the context of use and specify comprehensive user requirements, risking missed inputs that affect design decisions and iteration.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Because not all groups of users were directly involved in the design of T3, it is possible that important input may have been missed.

barriers.description: The design team struggled to decide which information elements to include due to diverse user roles and information needs.
barriers.justification: This cognitive/decision-making difficulty impeded the specification of clear user requirements and the production of stable design solutions, prolonging iterative design activities.
barriers.reference_excerpt: A challenge of the HCD process was deciding which information elements to include on T3, especially given the various users and roles with different information needs.

barriers.description: Nursing leadership concerns about the accuracy and safety of displayed information forced the team to add a proactive risk analysis step and raised issues about EHR data reliability and timely access.
barriers.justification: Stakeholder-driven requirements and data-source reliability constraints disrupted the planned HCD workflow and limited designers' ability to finalize requirements and iterate toward an implementable solution without resolving data/infrastructure dependencies.
barriers.reference_excerpt: We also discussed the impact of T3 on patient safety as nursing leaders expressed concern about the accuracy of the displayed information on T3. This led us to add a step in the HCD process and conduct a patient safety analysis (step 6).

barriers.description: Information-source reliability and timely access in the EHR were identified as important vulnerabilities for T3's data.
barriers.justification: Concerns about where data come from and EHR reliability constrained designers' ability to produce and evaluate an implementation-ready design, affecting specification of requirements and future integration/implementation work.
barriers.reference_excerpt: In a separate analysis, we found that about 90% of the information elements on T3 could be found in the EHR; the proactive risk analysis brought up the important issue of reliability of and timely access to information in the EHR.

barriers.description: The project produced and evaluated only a mock-up, so designers lacked information about real-world use of the technology.
barriers.justification: Absence of implementation prevented designers from conducting evaluation in actual workflow contexts, hindering the evaluate designs workload and the ability to refine designs based on real use.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Finally, because we developed and evaluated a technology mock-up, we do not have information on the actual use of the technology.
